meta.title: The AI Curve
meta.dataNote: Figures and claims are transcribed from the supplied October 2026 deck, not independently reverified. Intermediate values recovered from plotted geometry are rounded. Smooth connecting curves are visual guides, not additional observations or forecasts.

scene-ai-curve-opening.label: EXECUTIVE KEYNOTE / OCTOBER 2026
scene-ai-curve-opening.title: The AI curve.
paragraphs: This is a story about direction, not a catalogue of products. Capability is rising, the cost of intelligence is falling, and adoption is moving from experimentation into everyday work.
Read each curve as a leadership question: what becomes possible for our organization when this trend continues?
scene-ai-curve-opening.takeaway: Plan for the curve, not the snapshot.

scene-ai-curve-idea-map.label: 13 IDEAS / FOUR CHAPTERS
scene-ai-curve-idea-map.title: One story. Four movements.
paragraphs: Start with the underlying economics and capability shift. Follow the investment and demand signal. Then move from adoption to the redesign of work.
The source deck's two demand charts and three platform panels each have their own scene here, so every visual has room to breathe.

scene-ai-curve-task-horizon.label: IDEA 01 / CAPABILITY
scene-ai-curve-task-horizon.title: AI's working day is getting longer.
paragraphs: The measured horizon is the length of a task, expressed in the time a human expert would need, that a model completes with 50% probability. It is not the time the model runs, and not a promise of production reliability.
The deck reports a doubling time of about 89 days since 2024. The leadership implication is to design adaptable workflows, not to assume every task can already be delegated.
scene-ai-curve-task-horizon.takeaway: Plan for the curve, with explicit reliability gates.

scene-ai-curve-intelligence-price.label: IDEA 02 / ECONOMICS
scene-ai-curve-intelligence-price.title: Intelligence is becoming radically cheaper.
paragraphs: The source compares the cheapest available inference price at a fixed capability level, rather than the price of one unchanged model. Its GPT-4-level endpoints are $37.50 and $0.12 per million tokens.
That is about a 312-fold reduction. Governance, integration, evaluation and human oversight still cost money; lower inference cost is not the same as a free implementation.
scene-ai-curve-intelligence-price.takeaway: Revisit the economics. Keep the operating costs in view.

scene-ai-curve-build-out.label: IDEA 03 / INFRASTRUCTURE
scene-ai-curve-build-out.title: This is infrastructure. Not just a software cycle.
paragraphs: These are not like-for-like project budgets. The source compares nominal Big Tech capital expenditure with inflation-adjusted historic megaproject totals, using straight lines for the historic average pace.

The cumulative Big Tech trajectory follows the supplied source chart, starting from a zero origin. The dashed terminal segment includes guidance, not completed expenditure. Treat the comparison as a sense of scale, not a precise economic ranking.
scene-ai-curve-build-out.takeaway: The strategic question moves from infrastructure availability to organizational readiness.

scene-ai-curve-annual-capex.label: IDEA 04 / THE INVESTMENT SIGNAL
scene-ai-curve-annual-capex.title: Ten times the investment. Seven years.
paragraphs: The source reports $72 billion in 2019 and $733 billion guided for 2026. The ratio is just over ten times.
This includes the companies' entire capital expenditure. It should not be described as a pure measure of AI investment or proof of a return on that investment.
scene-ai-curve-annual-capex.takeaway: The scale of commitment is clear. The return still has to be earned.

scene-ai-curve-cloud-revenue.label: IDEA 05 / DEMAND, PART I
scene-ai-curve-cloud-revenue.title: Demand is moving into production.
paragraphs: This is the first of two visuals on source slide 7. It shows Microsoft Cloud quarterly revenue, not revenue attributable only to AI.
The source endpoints are $30.3 billion and $63.9 billion. Intermediate plotted values have been recovered from the original chart geometry and rounded to one decimal.
scene-ai-curve-cloud-revenue.takeaway: Growing demand is a signal to scale proven outcomes, not to skip evaluation.

scene-ai-curve-azure-growth.label: IDEA 05 / DEMAND, PART II
scene-ai-curve-azure-growth.title: Bigger. And accelerating.
paragraphs: This is the second visual on source slide 7, separated to make the distinction legible. Azure year-on-year growth and Microsoft Cloud absolute revenue are different measures.
The curve is not uninterrupted acceleration: it dips and recovers. The source shows a rise to 48% at the final point.
scene-ai-curve-azure-growth.takeaway: A stronger demand signal. Not a substitute for your own business case.

scene-ai-curve-billion-users.label: IDEA 06 / CONSUMER ADOPTION
scene-ai-curve-billion-users.title: One billion people. Every week.
paragraphs: The line shows weekly active users, as presented in the supplied deck. The commonly quoted 100 million users in two months is a different launch-era monthly-user measure and is deliberately not plotted as a weekly data point.
The organizational opportunity is not just access. It is approved tools, clear boundaries, training and a way to turn individual experimentation into repeatable value.
scene-ai-curve-billion-users.takeaway: Make governed work AI at least as usable as personal AI.

scene-ai-curve-daily-habit.label: IDEA 07 / THE HABIT CURVE
scene-ai-curve-daily-habit.title: A licence is not a habit. Daily use is.
paragraphs: The nested frequency groups should never be stacked or summed. Fifteen percent daily users sit within thirty percent weekly-or-more users, which sit within fifty-two percent any-use employees.
This is why a line comparison is more honest than a stacked area. The strategic question is what helps occasional use become a useful, safe working habit.
scene-ai-curve-daily-habit.takeaway: The useful KPI is sustained, outcome-producing use.

scene-ai-curve-business-chasm.label: IDEA 08 / ENTERPRISE ADOPTION
scene-ai-curve-business-chasm.title: The early majority is arriving.
paragraphs: The original source places its 9.7% point before the November 2025 question change, then 19.8% after it. This adaptation deliberately does not connect those points across the definition break.

The source's rhetorical increase from one in thirty to one in five mixes survey definitions. We preserve the reported values but make the comparability limit visible rather than implying an uninterrupted adoption curve.
scene-ai-curve-business-chasm.takeaway: Enterprise use is spreading. Compare definitions before comparing growth.

scene-ai-curve-nordic-lead.label: IDEA 09 / THE NORDIC LEAD
scene-ai-curve-nordic-lead.title: A head start. Not a finish line.
paragraphs: These are enterprise adoption percentages, not population use. The underlying population is businesses with at least ten employees.
Denmark and Sweden's 2023 values were derived in the source from reported year-on-year changes. Finland's trail begins in 2024 because the supplied graph does not plot an earlier observation.
scene-ai-curve-nordic-lead.takeaway: Turn adoption advantage into operating advantage.

scene-ai-curve-diffusion-race.label: IDEA 10 / DIFFUSION
scene-ai-curve-diffusion-race.title: Value follows diffusion. Not just invention.
paragraphs: The chart switches from enterprise adoption to working-age population diffusion. These measures are deliberately kept separate.
Sweden and the US begin at H2 2025 because no H1 observation is shown for them in the source graph. The periods have unequal duration, so this is a period comparison, not a growth-rate calculation.
scene-ai-curve-diffusion-race.takeaway: Spread capability widely enough for the economy of work to change.

scene-ai-curve-delegation.label: IDEA 11 / FROM HELPING TO DOING
scene-ai-curve-delegation.title: The crossing point is not the whole story.
paragraphs: The important nuance is visible in the final data point: augmentation returns to 52%, versus 45% automation, in November. The deck's crossing-point story should not be presented as an irreversible takeover.
The 77% business API figure is a separate population from Claude.ai conversations. Directive usage is a subtype and must not be added to the other lines.
scene-ai-curve-delegation.takeaway: Design for both collaboration and bounded delegation.

scene-ai-curve-beyond-it.label: IDEA 12 / A BUSINESS-WIDE CAPABILITY
scene-ai-curve-beyond-it.title: AI is leaving the IT department.
paragraphs: Computer and mathematical tasks remain the largest of the shown groups, while education and management gain share.

The education series stops before the others in the original visual. It is not extrapolated. The source's separate statement about spending outside enterprise IT is not encoded as conversation-share data.
scene-ai-curve-beyond-it.takeaway: AI ownership belongs across the business, not in one department.

scene-ai-curve-github-frontier.label: IDEA 13 / THE FRONTIER, PART I
scene-ai-curve-github-frontier.title: The developer frontier is compounding.
paragraphs: The source's first platform panel uses GitHub Copilot users. It grows from fifteen to fifty million across the shown disclosures.
Do not compare this absolute number directly with paid seats or customer organizations in the next panels. Each is a different population with its own zero-based scale.
scene-ai-curve-github-frontier.takeaway: Move from adoption volume to engineering impact.

scene-ai-curve-copilot-frontier.label: IDEA 13 / THE FRONTIER, PART II
scene-ai-curve-copilot-frontier.title: The knowledge-work frontier is scaling.
paragraphs: This is the source's second platform panel, separated from users and customer counts. The source reports paid seats rising from fifteen to thirty million.
Paid seats are an access measure. They should not be described as daily active usage, realized productivity or a verified business return.
scene-ai-curve-copilot-frontier.takeaway: Turn access into a habit, and the habit into a measurable outcome.

scene-ai-curve-foundry-frontier.label: IDEA 13 / THE FRONTIER, PART III
scene-ai-curve-foundry-frontier.title: The builder frontier is widening.
paragraphs: This is the source's third platform panel, measured in customer organizations. Seventy, one hundred and one hundred twenty thousand are the three plotted disclosures.
The broader Frontier Firm story connects platforms to data, governance and redesigned workflows. Platform growth alone does not demonstrate that every customer has achieved that operating model.
scene-ai-curve-foundry-frontier.takeaway: Build an operating capability, not a collection of pilots.

scene-ai-curve-close.label: THE CURVES ARE MOVING
scene-ai-curve-close.title: Where will you sit on the curve?
paragraphs: Every trend in the source deck points to a larger set of possibilities, but no curve makes the leadership decision for us.
Choose one valuable workflow, set a measurable outcome, establish boundaries and ownership, and build the organizational muscle to learn from the result.
scene-ai-curve-close.takeaway: Start with one outcome. Build for the curve.

scene-ai-curve-references.label: BEHIND EVERY LINE
scene-ai-curve-references.title: A story with its sources attached.
paragraphs: These are the references provided by the author of the source deck. Refer to the scene-specific source and caveat for the population, metric, timeframe and comparability limits.
Smooth curves are visual guides between source observations. They are not forecasts. Guidance is explicitly dashed and survey breaks are not joined.
scene-ai-curve-references.takeaway: Keep the evidence and its limits in the story.
